prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M; scope: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs, electrical up to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere: farm/transmission boundary, holds dispatch boundary, exchanges authorized signals, supply/protection status); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes authorized control, limits output, blocks protection-conflicting commands, reports state, safe mode on auxiliary loss; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (interlocks), Nacelle Condition Monitor (condition data: degradation vs transient), Turbine Sensor Bus (operating measurements). Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): imagery when vessel/rope access unjustified. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor (cable condition), station service transformers (essential/nonessential); sends Transformer Tap Snapshot on condition review request; Substation Operator confirms local constraints first. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-starts on auxiliary loss, transfers within V/f limits, no unapproved paralleling/export, sheds nonessential on overload, failure→alarm keeping UPS. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): status/alarms to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay: coordinates notices/interface, marine overview); flags work from Pitch Deviation Notice; produces Session Revocation Receipt. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): ranks work; uses Squall Window Bulletin. Duty Planner reviews ranked queue, confirms urgent work basis, selects mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), checks parts, competence, duration; Transfer Manifest Addendum. Priority: safety faults/major generation loss > routine; planned work advanced if justified; long-lead scheduled early. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): allocates output; assigns vessel/crew after Duty Planner priority; uses Position Quality Flag. Grid Dispatcher sets dispatch; frequency response only if authorized; comms loss keeps protection; alarms safety>protection>export. Field Supervisor validates faults, identifies offshore visits. Marine Coordinator: daily plan, compares access vs vessel capability, coordinates changes with Vessel Master. Crew Transfer Vessel (Kestrel Bay), SOV, Daughter Craft, Helideck, Port Agent, Rescue Coordinator, Operations Radio Console. Weather Service forecasts; Weather Analyst assesses confidence; Metocean Buoy (Copper Finch): Wave Burst Record; Weather Hold blocks mobilization beyond limits. Vessel AIS Receiver (Blue Granite): Position Quality Flag. Personnel Tracking Console, North/South Access

New part:
S269: The Duty Planner revises priorities when asset condition, access forecasts, or resource availability changes, and communicates the resulting plan to affected teams.
S270: Weather Service provides forecast conditions and confidence information for planned work areas and vessel routes.
S271: Metocean Buoy observations give the team a local reference for checking forecast trends and current sea state.
S272: Weather Analyst compares forecast data with recent observations before advising on the reliability of a work window.
S273: Forecast confidence is considered alongside the predicted conditions rather than treated as a substitute for operational limits.
S274: The Duty Planner checks that the expected conditions remain within the limits for the task, transfer method, and vessel.
S275: Low confidence near a limit leads to more conservative planning and a shorter review interval.
S276: A Weather Hold is applied when conditions are outside the approved limits or the available evidence is insufficient to support safe work.
S277: The Marine Coordinator reviews access options and vessel availability when a work window narrows.
S278: The Vessel Master receives the Transfer Manifest Addendum before departure.
S279: The Crew Transfer Vessel proceeds only when the Vessel Master considers the approach and transfer conditions acceptable.
S280: A forecast that improves does not by itself release a hold, because the team also checks current observations and the task-specific limits.
S281: The Service Operations Vessel may provide a more stable work platform, but its operating limits still govern whether work can proceed.
S282: Vessel Standby is used when transit or station keeping remains possible but personnel transfer or task execution is not justified.
S283: The Marine Coordinator reassesses the route when wind direction, wave conditions, or visibility changes materially.
S284: The Vessel Master can pause or abort an approach when observed conditions differ from the forecast or deteriorate during transit.
S285: Maintenance Planning Engine produces the Deferred Task Rationale when weather prevents a planned task from proceeding.
S286: The rationale supports later reprioritization without implying that the task is safe under the current conditions.
S287: Quiet Harbor blocks a route change when the required authorization is incomplete.
S288: Blue Granite provides vessel position information for review against the planned route and operating area.
S289: The team considers forecast uncertainty when deciding whether to commit crews, fuel, and vessel time to a remote work site.
S290: When conditions are changing rapidly, the Marine Coordinator seeks an updated forecast before confirming a departure or transfer plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
